actions.justification: Mandatory first step - assess current vital signs to determine hemodynamic stability and guide urgency of intervention in this patient with palpitations and dizziness.
Mandatory - 12-lead ECG is essential to identify the arrhythmia (e.g., atrial fibrillation, flutter, SVT) causing palpitations and dizziness, and guides all subsequent management decisions.
Mandatory - CHA2DS2-VASc score assessment is required to stratify stroke risk, especially relevant given hypertension as a comorbidity, and will guide anticoagulation decisions.
Mandatory lab order to assess electrolytes, renal function, and glucose — critical in evaluating palpitations and dizziness, and for guiding rate/rhythm management decisions.
Mandatory lab order to rule out thyroid dysfunction as a reversible cause of palpitations and potential arrhythmia (e.g., atrial fibrillation driven by hyperthyroidism).

Patient presenting with palpitations and dizziness warrants continuous cardiac monitoring to detect arrhythmia patterns, rate fluctuations, and any hemodynamic deterioration while awaiting lab results.

Patient has hypertension (a CHA2DS2-VASc risk factor) and palpitations/dizziness suggesting possible atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc score has been assessed; now formally evaluate anticoagulation need based on that score and clinical context before initiating any treatment.

Patient presenting with palpitations and dizziness with comorbid hypertension warrants cardiology consultation for further evaluation and management guidance, particularly regarding rhythm vs. rate control strategy and anticoagulation decisions.

Patient with palpitations and dizziness with history of hypertension warrants electrophysiology consultation to further evaluate arrhythmia etiology after initial ECG and labs have been ordered. EP can guide further workup and management decisions.

Order follow-up ECG to assess current rhythm and document any changes since initial 12-lead ECG, supporting identification of the clinical syndrome (e.g., atrial fibrillation, flutter, SVT) governing treatment decisions.

Echocardiogram is indicated to assess cardiac structure and function, identify valvular disease, wall motion abnormalities, or structural causes of palpitations and arrhythmia in this hypertensive patient.

Chest X-ray is indicated to evaluate for structural cardiac or pulmonary causes of palpitations and dizziness, and to assess for cardiomegaly, pulmonary edema, or other abnormalities in this hypertensive patient with pending workup.

Echocardiogram to evaluate cardiac structure and function, assess for structural heart disease contributing to palpitations/arrhythmia in this hypertensive patient. Note: order_echocardiogram was listed as already done but order_imaging_echocardiogram is a distinct available action ID in this scenario's list.

If the working diagnosis is atrial fibrillation/flutter with palpitations and dizziness, rate control is a standard initial management step. Vitals are currently stable (HR 80, BP 120/80) but rate control may be needed depending on rhythm confirmation.

Patient has hypertension (CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥1) and palpitations/dizziness suggestive of atrial fibrillation. Anticoagulation assessment has been completed; initiating anticoagulation is appropriate to reduce thromboembolic risk per AF guidelines.
CBC is indicated to evaluate for anemia, infection, or other hematologic causes contributing to palpitations and dizziness in this patient.
Renal function assessment is essential for safe medication dosing (rate control, anticoagulation) and to evaluate for electrolyte-related arrhythmia contributors in a hypertensive patient.
Coagulation studies are important to monitor anticoagulation therapy that has already been initiated and to establish baseline coagulation status.
NT-proBNP can help assess for underlying heart failure or structural heart disease contributing to palpitations and arrhythmia, which is relevant given the cardiac workup in progress.
INR monitoring is important to assess anticoagulation status, especially since anticoagulation has already been initiated. Ensures therapeutic range and safety.
Lactate helps assess for hypoperfusion or hemodynamic compromise despite currently stable vitals, providing additional safety information during the workup.

Troponin should be ordered to evaluate for myocardial injury or ischemia as a potential trigger or complication of the arrhythmia presenting as palpitations and dizziness, and has not yet been completed.

Patient with likely atrial fibrillation (palpitations/dizziness, hypertension) who has already received rate control and anticoagulation. IV amiodarone is indicated for pharmacological rhythm control/cardioversion in hemodynamically stable AF when other rate/rhythm control measures have been initiated.
Additional rate control with beta blocker may be beneficial to ensure adequate heart rate control in a hypertensive patient with likely AF, complementing existing rate control therapy if needed.
